summary: The study investigates the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of molybdenum nitride (MoNx) using Mo(CO)6 and NH3 as precursors for Cu diffusion barrier applications. The process is carried out within a temperature range of 180–300 °C, with the optimal ALD temperature window identified as 200–215 °C. The films deposited at higher temperatures exhibit improved properties, such as higher density and lower resistivity, making them effective Cu diffusion barriers. The study also explores the effects of post-annealing and the use of NH3 plasma on the film properties.
evidence: Deposition providing precise control of the film thickness, low deposition temperature, and non-corrosive by-products is essential for the efficient fabrication of barrier layers in semiconductor devices. Here, molybdenum nitride (MoNx) is deposited for Cu diffusion barrier application at a relatively low temperature (180–300 °C) by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using molybdenum hexacarbonyl [Mo(CO)6)] and ammonia gas (NH3).
